title: Ella Fitzgerald, Big Joe Turner and Basie men sit in at the Victoria
summary: Ella sang A Tisket A Tasket, Turner and Basie band members sat in from the nearby Woodside Hotel.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Now, Kirby came in to hear you... Oh, before we go back over that: At the Victoria Cafe, did any singers ever ask you if they could sit in and sing a number or two?
Well, one of them was Ella Fitzgerald.
Oh, Ella?
Moore (III) - 9
She was working at the Savoy.
She must have been very young then.

Yeah, she was. She was at the Savoy with Chick Webb. Right across the street on the next corner is where the Savoy was. So she'd come in to sit in, sing a number like "A Tisket, A Tasket," which made her famous, you know, and other numbers she'd sing...

Big Joe Turner, the Blues singer, he used to sit in. I think he'd come there to New York with Count Basie. The whole band stopped at the Woodside Hotel, right next to the Victoria Cafe. Count Basie come in town with Big Joe Turner, they called him. He was a Blues singer with Count Basie's band.
So did some of the Basie Band musicians ever come in to hear you?
Yeah, they used to come there and sit in.
Sit in?
Yeah, they'd in some nights. They got to keep their chops together -- the horn blowers, you know.
I see. People like Hershel....?
Hershel, yeah, and I think...
Lester?
Let's see... If I'm not mistaken, I think Hot Lips Page was with that band.
Moore (III) - 10
Hot Lips Page.
Yeah.
How about...? Of course, I think Sweets and Buck Clayton were also... How about Freddie Green? Did he ever come over and sit in with you?

Freddie would come in once in a while. He was a big rhythm man. He'd keep that band together. He'd sat right aside the drummer and keep the band together, keep the tempo, keep the rhythm right together. He wasn't very much of a soloist. He'd just get a rhythm going to keep the band together.
